content:
Limits look like plug-and-play until the form goes 0/0. Then you need the standard limits, not a calculator. That single skill decides your calculus score. Take the free JEE Limits and Continuity online test below. It has 15 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring. Aim for 12 out of 15.

What JEE asks from limits

  • Algebraic limits using factor and rationalise tricks.
  • Trigonometric limits built on sin x over x.
  • Exponential and logarithmic standard limits.
  • Limits at infinity for rational functions.
  • Continuity and differentiability at a joint point.

Standard limits to revise first

  • The limit of sin x over x is 1, as x goes to 0.
  • The limit of (a^x − 1) over x equals ln a.
  • Also (1 − cos x) over x² tends to 1/2.
  • For (x^n − 1) over (x − 1), the limit is n at x = 1.
  • A function stays continuous when both side limits meet its value.

Mistakes that cost JEE marks

  • Applying L Hopital before checking the 0/0 form.
  • Cancelling a factor that is not really common.
  • Forgetting that a jump discontinuity breaks differentiability.

How to use this test

Put 30 minutes on a clock. Do the standard limits first. Those are quick wins. Then tackle the tricky forms. Write each step by hand. Do not skip a line. Spot the 0/0 form before you act. Pick the right standard limit. If a value looks odd, redo it once. Mark every slip you make. Try the set again in two days. Your speed will rise, and your errors will drop.

quiz.title: JEE Limits and Continuity Quiz
quiz.intro: Fifteen exam-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: JEE Maths DPP: Limits and Continuity

questions.explanation: Write 2^(3+h) = 8·2^h, so the expression is 8(2^h − 1)/h. As h → 0 the ratio tends to log 2, giving 8 log 2.

questions.q: Evaluate lim(x→π/4) (sin x − cos x)/(x − π/4).
questions.explanation: The numerator equals √2 sin(x − π/4). Using sin θ / θ → 1, the limit is √2.
Divide top and bottom by x. The numerator tends to 1 and the denominator to log 3, giving log(e)/log(3).
Expand e^x = 1 + x + x²/2 + …, so e^x − 1 − x = x²/2 + …. Dividing by x² gives 1/2.
Let y = π/2 − x, so 1 − sin x = 1 − cos y. Then (1 − cos y)/y² → 1/2.
Use 1 − cos x = 2 sin²(x/2). The limit reduces to 1/2.

questions.q: If lim(x→1) (x⁴ − 1)/(x − 1) = lim(x→k) (x³ − k³)/(x² − k²), then k equals:
questions.explanation: The left side is 4. The right side simplifies to (3/2)k. Setting 4 = (3/2)k gives k = 8/3.
Both are degree two, so the limit is the ratio of leading coefficients, which is 3/2.
Multiply by the conjugate to get x/[√(x² + x) + x]. Dividing by x gives 1/2.
Rewrite as (7/2)·(tan 7x)/(7x). Since tan θ / θ → 1, the limit is 7/2.
The standard limit (a^x − 1)/x → log a gives log 2 for a = 2.
Use (1 − cos ax)/x² → a²/2. With a = 3 the value is 9/2.
Rationalise the numerator to reach 1/[√(2 + x) + √2]. At x = 0 this is 1/(2√2).

questions.q: Let g(x) = |f(x)| for all x. Which property does g inherit from f?
questions.explanation: The absolute value of a continuous function stays continuous. Onto, one-one and differentiability need not carry over.

questions.q: Which function is differentiable at x = 0?
questions.explanation: For x|x| the left and right derivatives at 0 both equal 0. The others have a corner at 0.
